title: Locations and numbers
blurb: Locations hold dialing habits, the main number, and the PSTN connection. Numbers and extensions live there.

lessons.title: What a location is
lessons.summary: A Webex Calling location is the site container: time zone, dialing, main number, and one PSTN connection. It is not a Unified CM device pool, even when you migrate from one.
objectives: List what dialing settings it holds

diagram.caption: Users and numbers hang off a location. The PSTN connection is a property of that location.

steps.label: Add the main number
steps.detail: The location main number is the default face of the site.

steps.label: Then connect
steps.detail: Only after the location exists. Premises PSTN also needs a trunk created first.

paragraphs: Migration Insights can group numbers by device pool, but the destination object is a Webex Calling location. People who share a device pool do not automatically share a location.
Decide locations by PSTN, dialing habits, and emergency address, not by the old cluster's device-pool name alone.

fault.title: One location for a country
fault.symptom: A national main number hides three different street addresses, and 933 returns the wrong floor.
fault.log: SYNTHETIC: 933 test, expected dock, got HQ lobby.
fault.cause: Dispatchable location is per place. One Control Hub location with one address cannot describe three buildings.

lessons.title: Extension length, prefix, and the external digit
lessons.summary: Internal dialing is extension length and routing prefix. The external digit is the habit people already have. These are location settings, tested in the dial-plan simulator.
lessons.uncertainty: Cisco documents the dialing controls. This lab's simulator order is explicitly a teaching model.
objectives: Know the simulator is a teaching model

diagram.caption: 2100 stays inside the site. 222100 crosses to the site whose prefix is 22.

steps.label: Dial 2100
steps.detail: If the extension length is 4, the simulator treats 2100 as an extension in this location.

steps.label: Dial prefix plus extension
steps.detail: A dial string that starts with another location's routing prefix, with the remainder equal to that extension length, stays inside Webex Calling.

steps.label: Dial 9 then the number
steps.detail: The external digit is stripped when the remainder is long enough to be an outside number.
steps.inspect: Not a global law. A location setting.

steps.label: Read the trace
steps.detail: The trace names the rule and the article. Precedence is labeled as a lab model.

paragraphs: The organization article says you customize extension lengths, routing prefixes, and internal and external dialing preferences so they match existing habits.
It does not publish a single worldwide external digit. If a design assumes 9 everywhere, write that assumption down.

cite.label: Configure Webex Calling for your organization

paragraphs: The lab simulator strips one configured external digit, matches extension length, then routing prefixes, then +E.164 patterns. Cisco's articles describe the objects, not this exact evaluation order.
Use the trace to learn the objects. Confirm order in Control Hub when you build a real plan.

fault.title: Prefix collision
fault.symptom: Users in site 21 reach the wrong building when they dial 2100.
fault.log: SYNTHETIC: location Austin prefix 21, Richmond extensions also start with 21, length 4.
fault.cause: A routing prefix that is also the start of a local extension is ambiguous in the teaching model and painful in production.
fault.fix: Give each location a prefix that is not a local extension, and retest both dials.

lessons.title: Main numbers, caller ID, and ports
lessons.summary: Ordering and porting numbers depends on the PSTN choice. Cisco Calling Plan can order or port. CCP partners and premises carriers do it on their own contracts.
objectives: Match the number source to the PSTN model
Do not port a number in a simulator

diagram.caption: The PSTN provider, not Control Hub alone, owns the port order.

flow.title: Add a number to a location

steps.label: Read the contract
steps.detail: Cisco Calling Plan is Cisco as the cloud PSTN, including number orders and ports where the plan is offered.

steps.label: Or a partner
steps.detail: Cloud Connected PSTN is a partner when you want that coverage or when Cisco Calling Plan is not offered.

steps.label: Keep the carrier
steps.detail: Premises PSTN keeps the current provider. Numbers stay on that carrier and arrive through the local gateway.

steps.label: Assign
steps.detail: Put the number on the location and then on a user, workspace, or feature.

paragraphs: The organization article describes Cisco PSTN as Cisco's cloud PSTN with emergency calling, inbound and outbound calling, and the ability to order or port numbers.
CCP is the cloud alternative from a partner. Premises PSTN keeps your provider or connects non-cloud sites. Pick the source before you promise a port date.

sections.h: Caller ID is not the ECBN
paragraphs: The number people see on an ordinary outbound call is caller ID. The number emergency services see for callback is the ECBN, chosen from the line number, the location default, or another user or virtual line in the same location.
Changing caller ID does not by itself change the emergency callback number.

lessons.title: Calling between locations
lessons.summary: On-net calls between Webex Calling locations use routing prefixes and extensions. They are not PSTN calls, and they do not need the local gateway.
objectives: Keep on-net calls off the PSTN
Spot a prefix that matches an extension

diagram.caption: Site prefix plus extension stays inside Webex Calling.

steps.label: Dial 222100
steps.detail: Prefix 22 selects Austin. 2100 is the extension.

steps.label: Ring the user
steps.detail: Both users are Webex Calling destinations, so the call does not fall through to the local gateway.
steps.inspect: Workflow: unmatched calls are the ones that leave

steps.label: Dial back
steps.detail: The return prefix is 21. One-way prefixes are a classic fault.

steps.label: Confirm on-net
steps.detail: A PSTN carrier record for this call means the prefix was not recognized.

paragraphs: The workflow guide sends calls that are not Webex Calling destinations to the local gateway. Another location's user is a Webex Calling destination once the dialing habit resolves.

fault.title: Hairpin to the carrier
fault.symptom: Site-to-site calls show up on the PSTN bill.
fault.log: SYNTHETIC: carrier CDR, called=222100, no Webex location prefix 22.
fault.cause: 22 was never configured as Austin's routing prefix, so Webex Calling did not treat it as on-net.
fault.fix: Set the routing prefix, republish dialing, and place one call each way. Confirm the carrier CDR stops.

fault.title: Beautiful caller ID, no callback
fault.symptom: Marketing sets caller ID to a main number that cannot be called back, and ECBN follows it by mistake.
fault.log: SYNTHETIC: ECBN=800 main, queue closed, PSAP callback fails.
fault.cause: ECBN has to reach a person. A published main number that lands on a closed attendant fails the callback.
fault.fix: Set ECBN to the line or to a staffed number in the same location. Place a test with the carrier's method, and 933 if RedSky is on.

lessons.summary: Virtual lines and shared lines are Professional features in the license matrix. They change how a number appears, and they change emergency behavior.
